contributions.summary: Computes GGDP and RGG for 46 countries, showing developed countries have higher greenness.
Fuzzy comprehensive evaluation shows climate scores improve from (0.25,0.76,0.38) to (0.71,1.28,0.38) with GGDP.
Game theory shows all opponents accept GGDP within 15 years.
Time dimension shows $51.6T additional income over 40 years.
PVAR shows tertiary industry contributes 47.27% vs 21.07% for secondary in Australia.

dependency_graph.handoff: RGG and cost components feed into fuzzy evaluation
Climate mitigation evidence motivates the game and time analysis
Australia's RGG identifies it as a high-pollution adopter

assumptions.summary: Countries plan strictly according to GGDP criteria after adoption.
No sudden global events within the forecast horizon.
Energy structure and resource efficiency stable in short term.

data_and_preprocessing.summary: 46 countries, World Bank and OECD, 1995-2020, 7 indicators. Linear interpolation for missing ECO2 and Waste.

models.summary: GGC: Stjepanovic-based GGDP formula and RGG.
FCE: Three-level fuzzy comprehensive evaluation with AHP weights.
GAM: Spatial game theory plus time-dimension carrying capacity.
PVA: PVAR for Australia's industry structure.

verification.summary: Fuzzy scores improve in all three dimensions.
All 5 opposing countries accept by year 15.
Unit root tests significant at 1%, all eigenvalues in unit circle.

results_trace.summary: RGG higher in developed countries, lower in resource-exporting countries.
Climate scores increase toward (2,2,2) with GGDP.

writing_logic.summary: Abstract uses 'For Task N' blocks, same pattern as paper 424.
Imagine-map opener contrasts beauty with disaster.
Section title 'It's time to make the right choice' is a call to action.
Memo uses 'To whom it may concern' and 'Yours Sincerely' formal register.

language_observations.summary: 'Imagine a map... what comes to mind is not [beauty]; it is [disasters]' is a vivid contrast opener.
'it is a question to ponder whether GGDP is the most appropriate option' closes with genuine uncertainty.
Triangle bullet (▷) Justification format is a distinctive visual marker.
'The highlight of this method is that it introduces' names the winning trait directly.
Section title as imperative call: 'It's time to make the right choice'.
'We must take into account the contribution they once made when the rules no longer change in their favor' is an equity argument.
'no country can rest on its laurels' is a memorable idiom.
'which may seem like a challenge, but it will be well worth it' is a concession-then-reassurance.

judge_relevance_hypotheses.summary: Game theory framing makes the adoption argument rigorous rather than rhetorical.
PVAR provides quantitative backing for the claim that industrial transformation is feasible.

weaknesses.summary: Does not consider water, land, or biodiversity in environmental analysis.
Subjective element in future policy impact curve.
Loss curves assumed, not fitted to actual disaster data.

independent_extensions.summary: Fit loss curves to actual natural disaster GDP-loss data rather than assuming.
Report AHP consistency ratio and test with entropy weighting as a robustness check.

candidate_rule_impacts.summary: Game-theoretic framing of adoption turns a policy question into a formal equilibrium problem.
Distinguishing actual cost from opportunity cost in the GGDP formula.

unresolved_questions.question: What is the exact value of a in the loss curve Ln=at?
How are f and b calibrated in the benefit equation?
